one_liner: Cython bindings to the Lexbor/Modest C HTML5 engines, giving CSS-selector DOM parsing faster than lxml/libxml2.
what_it_does: selectolax wraps two standalone C HTML5 parsing engines (Modest and Lexbor) in Cython, exposing a DOM tree you query with CSS selectors (`.css()`, `.css_first()`) plus `.text()`/`.attributes` accessors. It targets read-heavy scraping tasks — pulling titles, links, and specific attributes out of HTML — not general document manipulation. It is not a drop-in for lxml or BeautifulSoup: you pick `HTMLParser` (Modest) or `LexborHTMLParser` (Lexbor) and use selectolax's own method names, not XPath.
how_it_is_fast: The speedup comes from parsing in native, purpose-built HTML5 engines (Modest, and its successor Lexbor) rather than through libxml2's more general-purpose parser/tree machinery that lxml wraps, or Python-level parsing in BeautifulSoup's html.parser backend. Cython binds directly to the C node structures for traversal and CSS matching instead of materializing a heavier Python object per node. The published benchmark exercises light extraction (title, `a[href]`, script count, one meta tag) over 754 pages, not full tree mutation or serialization, so the win is concentrated in parse + shallow query, not general DOM editing.
when_to_use: Scraping/extraction pipelines that are CPU-bound on parsing large volumes of HTML and only need to read specific fields, not mutate the tree heavily
You're fine writing to selectolax's own CSS-selector API instead of XPath or BeautifulSoup's find/find_all
You want HTML5-spec error recovery (like a browser) without a full browser or html5lib
You explicitly use the Lexbor backend (`LexborHTMLParser`) rather than the legacy Modest one
when_not_to_use: You need a free-threaded (no-GIL) Python build — support is requested but still open (issue #215, opened 2026-03-18)
Workload is XPath-driven or needs heavy DOM mutation/serialization — the verified benchmark only covers read-only field extraction
You want the Modest backend for new code — the project itself says the underlying Modest C library is unmaintained and steers users to Lexbor

You can't tolerate native-extension crash risk — past segfault under sustained load with `strip_tags()`+`text()` (#217) and memory corruption when deleting attributes (#172), both since fixed but indicative of the risk class
You need XPath support at all — selectolax is CSS-selectors only, with a nonstandard `:lexbor-contains()` pseudo-class as its one extension

integration.dependencies: none at runtime; Cython + setuptools>=62.4 needed only to build from source (wheels ship prebuilt)
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS, Windows (per PyPI classifiers); no free-threaded/no-GIL build yet
integration.thread_safety: not documented in README; free-threaded Python support is an open, unresolved issue (#215)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: same job as lxml.html.fromstring (parse + query HTML), but different classes (HTMLParser/LexborHTMLParser) and CSS-selector-only API instead of XPath, so call sites must be rewritten

gotchas: Two backends (Modest, Lexbor) with overlapping but not identical features; Lexbor is the recommended one since 2024 but isn't used by every example/class by default — check which parser you import
Backend licenses differ from the package license: Modest is LGPL-2.1 and Lexbor is Apache-2.0, even though selectolax itself is MIT

Native-extension bugs have caused a SIGSEGV under sustained load (`strip_tags()`+`text()`, v0.4.8, issue #217) and memory corruption when deleting attributes (issue #172) — both closed/fixed, but crashes bypass normal Python exception handling
No XPath; only CSS selectors plus the Lexbor-specific `:lexbor-contains()` pseudo-class for text matching
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick selectolax over raw lexbor when you want a maintained, widely-used (1.68k stars) Python package instead of hand-rolling FFI bindings to the C library yourself. Pick it over html5-parser when you don't need the output as an lxml tree — html5-parser deliberately produces an lxml-compatible tree so you can keep using XPath, which selectolax does not support. MarkupEver's published numbers are on microsecond-scale document sizes versus this benchmark's multi-second, 324MB corpus, so the two aren't directly comparable without testing on your own data.
verified_claims_summary: On a 324MB corpus of 754 top-domain homepages (extracting title, `a[href]`s, script-tag count, and meta description), selectolax(Lexbor) ran in 2.39s and selectolax(Modest) in 2.94s versus lxml.html.fromstring+XPath used directly at 9.09s (~3.8x and ~3.1x faster respectively) and BeautifulSoup(html.parser) at 61.02s. This is a single wall-clock run with no CPU, compiler, or flags stated, and the corpus itself is unpublished due to copyright.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-09-24, CI passing, Python 3.9-3.14 support) and MIT-licensed, but the bundled Modest engine is itself unmaintained upstream, so new code should target the Lexbor backend; free-threaded-Python support remains an open request.
